answer: In Barcelona province (Catalonia, NE Spain), urban land use promoted the invasion of non-native plants introduced UNINTENTIONALLY (via global trade and tourism) — predominantly ruderal ANNUAL weeds — in the scenario of urbanized landscapes: plots located in the Urban habitat and in surroundings with high CURRENT urban cover in the 500–1000 m buffers, whose urbanization occurred mainly from 1956 onward (current/2009 urban cover is the operative driver, OR per +1 SD ≈ 1.9–2.0–2.5, p<1e-6; pre-1956 historical cover is not). Specifically, unintentional-pathway non-natives were the type most strongly promoted: their plot-level PRESENCE odds rose with 2009 urban cover (OR per +1 SD = 1.83 at 50 m, 2.01 at 500 m, 1.92 at 1000 m; all p<1e-6) and their counts rose ~1.4–1.5× per +1 SD (negative-binomial IRR, p<1e-4); they dominated the Urban habitat (mean 1.60 species/plot, presence 75%, vs 0.33/17% non-urban). Head-to-head, the gardening (ornamental) pathway was much more weakly and inconsistently associated with urban cover (OR ≈1.2–1.4, significant at 500 m only, p=0.008; ~0 at 50/1000 m) and agri-forestry showed none — and among invaded plots the unintentional share of occurrences rose with urban cover while the gardening share fell (p≈0.01). Although gardening dominates recent INTRODUCTION trends (75% of since-1985 introductions; chi² p=6e-47), it is precisely the contrast type, not the one promoted by urban land use. These unintentionally introduced invaders are also the region's most successful non-natives (highest number of invaded plots, area of occupancy, habitat range and invaded niche breadth), e.g. Erigeron sumatrensis, Amaranthus retroflexus, Symphyotrichum squamatum, Erigeron canadensis, and are phylogenetically concentrated in Asteraceae/Amaranthaceae (weak/equivocal corroboration).

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use promoted the invasion of non-native plants introduced UNINTENTIONALLY (via global trade/tourism; ruderal annual weeds) in the scenario of urbanized landscapes — Urban habitat and surroundings with high current (2009) urban cover at 500–1000 m buffers, resulting from post-1956 urbanization — with this type promoted specifically (presence OR up to ~2.0 per +1 SD urban, p<1e-6; NB IRR ~1.5, p<1e-4) and much more strongly than gardening/agriforest species.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected all four files (dimensions, NAs, dups, integrity). 2) Temporal trend chi-square (context only). 3) Validated progressive/regressive change vars against computed 1956–2009 urban/cropland deltas (labels found REVERSED). 4) Presence-logit and Poisson/NB count models per pathway × buffer (50/500/1000 m) with covariates (cropland, elevation, log distance road/stream, temperature, rainfall). 5) Scenario test: urban_1956 vs urban_2009 in one model. 6) Head-to-head type discrimination: per-pathway ORs, compositional share of unintentional and log(gard/unint) vs urban among the 191 invaded plots. 7) Species-level trait corroboration. 8) Phylogeny: custom Newick parser, pairwise patristic distances vs random expectation (reported equivocal). 9) Count-model validation: Poisson vs NB (LR, alpha) vs ZIP/ZINB (AIC; instability reported).
